land.text: Land (Upper) Chenla north of the Tonlé Sap and along the Mekong, taken in Jayavarman II's unification

predecessors.note: The Khmer Empire page lists 'Lower Chenla; Upper Chenla' as predecessors. The pages opened do not say when each part joined; 803 is a bridge (Land Chenla's own dossier is drawn through 802).

land.text: Water (Lower) Chenla in the south, up to the Mekong delta

predecessors.note: The Jayavarman II page: Java 'invaded and conquered the Water Chenla and beheaded Mahipativarman', after which Jayavarman II was installed; he later united the kingdoms. Year bridged to 803.

land.text: the Khmer realm that remained after 1375: the Tonlé Sap basin and the Mekong lands, with the court at Phnom Penh (Chaktomuk) after Angkor was abandoned

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Post-Angkor Cambodia'. The Khmer Empire page: in 1431 Ponhea Yat 'abandoned Angkor as indefensible' and moved to the Phnom Penh area. Cliopatria keeps its 'Khmer Empire' row going to 1867; the 1432-1863 part is the separate dossier post-angkor-cambodia.

land.text: the northern Khmer lands that Cliopatria hands to Lan Xang in 1363

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Lan Xang' (founded 1353 per the infobox); the handover is earlier than 1431, in 1363 on Cliopatria's shapes.

land.text: the western strip that Cliopatria hands to Ayutthaya in 1375

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Ayutthaya'; the page dates sieges of Angkor in 1352-53 and 1393-94 but no cession of land.

capitals.name: Mahendraparvata (Phnom Kulen)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Mahendraparvata (early 9th century)'. The 802 consecration was on Phnom Kulen. The year the court left for Hariharalaya is not on the pages; 834 is a bridge.

capitals.name: Hariharalaya (Roluos)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Hariharalaya (mid 9th century)'; the Jayavarman II page: 'founded Hariharalaya near present-day Roluos'. Span bridged between the two infobox phrases.

capitals.name: Yasodharapura (Angkor)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Yasodharapura (late 9th century-928)'; founded under Yasovarman I (reigned 889-915), centred on Phnom Bakheng.

capitals.name: Lingapura (Koh Ker)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Lingapura (928-944)'; the text says Jayavarman IV moved it 'at the beginning of the 10th century', about 100 km northeast of Angkor. Coordinates are the site of Koh Ker.

capitals.name: Yasodharapura (Angkor)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Yasodharapura (944-1431)'; restored as the capital in 944 by Rajendravarman II. Jayendranagari (Jayavarman V) and Angkor Thom (Jayavarman VII, year not given) are new centres at the same site.

correction.text: the core around Phnom Kulen and the country north of the Tonlé Sap, unchanged, for 802 only

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws a 5,340 km2 core around Phnom Kulen and Angkor from 800; the Jayavarman II page puts the consecration at Mahendraparvata 'in 802' and the Khmer Empire page says the empire 'lasted from 802 to 1431'. The shape is kept for 802 only (the birth frame); from 803 the Chenla lands join (see khmer-empire_806).

correction.text: the union of Land and Water Chenla, unchanged, for 803-874

keyframe_review.note: 450,000 km2 for 806-874; by gazetteer it contains all of Land Chenla's and Water Chenla's last Cliopatria shapes (1,418 cells) plus 97 more cells. The page is silent on when the Chenla lands joined (he returned 'to his home in the former kingdom of Chenla' and defeated 'a series of competing kings', undated), so the shape is kept but dated from 803, the year after Land Chenla's own dossier ends (802), instead of 806. About 45,800 km2 of its eastern edge (the highlands and coast between 106.9 and 109 E, 10.5-15.2 N) also lies inside Cliopatria's Champa shape of 875 (see the 875 loss). No infobox area for this period.

397,553 km2, the 806 shape without the eastern strip that Cliopatria gives to Champa in 875. The Khmer-Cham wars page treats Kauthara and Panduranga as Cham-held and has the c. 950 Khmer raid on Kauthara end in defeat, so the shrunken shape agrees with the later pages; it is silent on 875 itself. Years: 875-1005 (the Lavo shape takes over from 1006).

540,563 km2: the 875 shape plus 475 cells that lie wholly inside Cliopatria's Lavo shape (473 of 475 inside Lavo 1056; Lavo disappears from Cliopatria in 1028-1055). The Suryavarman I page: he 'expanded his territory to the west to Lopburi' and into 'the Menam basin', no year; his reign is 1006-1050 on the infobox ('Suryavarman I claimed the throne in 1010'). The shape is kept but dated 1006-1051, to match Lavo's own dossier (loss to Angkor 1006, return 1052) instead of Cliopatria's 1028-1055.
397,553 km2, identical to the 875 shape: Lavo has left. 'Suryavarman died in 1050' (page); the page is silent on 1052. Dated 1052-1110.

Same 397,553 km2 outline as 1056 for 1111-1187. Dated 1111-1180: Jayavarman VII's accession in 1181 puts Lavo back under Angkor (new keyframe khmer-empire_1181). No event on the pages opened changes the frontier between 1052 and 1180: Suryavarman II's wars (1127-1149) reached Nghệ An and Vijaya but held ground only briefly or by occupation.

correction.text: the 1111 shape plus Lavo, Lopburi, under Angkor from the coronation of Jayavarman VII

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from the coronation of Jayavarman VII ('in 1181 was crowned king himself') the outline is the 1111 shape plus Lavo, which the Jayavarman VII page lists among the 23 towns of his reign ('Among them were Lavo (modern Lopburi)'). The year is the reign's start, a bridge; Cliopatria draws the larger shape only from 1188.

830,253 km2 against the infobox's 1,000,000 km2 for 1181-1218 (ratio 0.83, within a factor of two). Gazetteer: the step from 1111 adds 1,470 cells, 465 of them Lavo and 295 Haripunjaya's southern lands, the rest stateless uplands. The page says only that he 'expanded Khmer control of the Mekong Valley northward to Vientiane' and 'southward down the Kra Isthmus', and that Champa was a dependency 'for 30 years'; Cliopatria's northern edge (21.2 N) lies far beyond Vientiane (18.0 N) and nothing on the pages supports it, so that part is unverified. Shape kept, dated 1188-1202 (the Champa conquest follows).

953,197 km2: the 1188 shape plus all of Champa (410 of 411 added cells are Cliopatria's Champa shape). 'Champa became a Khmer province ruled by a puppet government' from 1203 to 1220, so the shape is dated 1203-1217 instead of Cliopatria's 1206-1219; infobox 1,000,000 km2 (ratio 0.95). Lavo leaves in 1218 (next keyframe).

minus.text: Lavo, as Cliopatria's 1241 Lavo shape draws it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 1218-1219, the 1206 shape without Lavo. 'Jayavarman died around 1218' and the Lavo dossier ends Angkor's governorship that year; the pages opened do not say what happened to Lavo, so the year is a bridge. Champa is still a Khmer province until the 1220 evacuation.

minus.text: Lavo, as Cliopatria's 1241 Lavo shape draws it

keyframe_review.note: 830,253 km2, the 1188 shape. the Khmer 'voluntarily evacuated Champa' in 1220, which returns the Cham coast, as the shape shows; Lavo has left since 1218, so Lavo is subtracted. Dated 1220-1237 (Sukhothai breaks away in 1238).

minus.text: Lavo, as Cliopatria's 1241 Lavo shape draws it

keyframe_review.note: Identical outline to the 1220 shape (830,253 km2); the two are folded together: without Lavo, for 1227-1237. Nothing on the pages opened changes the frontier in 1227.

515,874 km2: the step down from 830,253 is 1,059 cells, 916 of them exactly Cliopatria's Sukhothai shape of 1241 and 143 Lavo's. Sukhothai 'is conventionally regarded as having emerged as an independent polity in 1238', so the shape is dated from 1238. The page also says the old reading of 1238 as 'the liberation of Sukhothai from Khmer suzerainty' is contested (no Angkorian inscriptions on the Chao Phraya plain). Dated 1238-1313.

515,787 km2, the 1241 outline; no event on the pages opened moves the frontier in 1314 (the infobox lists none). A 'recent war with the Siamese' is reported by Zhou Daguan in August 1296, without a date or a land change.
515,985 km2, the same outline. Uthong's siege (1352) and capture of Angkor (1353) are drawn as an occupation (1353-1357), not a change of border; the Khmer king returned in 1357.

304,078 km2: the north (731 of the 733 cells lost) is exactly Cliopatria's Lan Xang of 1363. The Khmer Empire page says Fa Ngum, exiled at Angkor, 'received a Khmer army to create a buffer state in Laos' and gives 'Lan Xang founded: 1353'; it does not say the Khmer ceded land, so the loss in 1363 is Cliopatria's date (conf 1 in the ledger).

240,474 km2: the strip lost since 1363 (212 of 215 cells) lies inside Cliopatria's Ayutthaya shape of 1375. The page dates sieges of Angkor in 1352-53 and 1393-94 but no cession in 1375 (conf 1). Years for this dossier: 1375-1431; the post-Angkor dossier takes 1432-1474 of the same shape.

region.text: the core around Mahendraparvata (Phnom Kulen) and the country north of the Tonlé Sap

ledger.note: 802: Jayavarman II is consecrated at Mahendraparvata (Phnom Kulen) and the Khmer Empire begins. the page says he was proclaimed 'devaraja' at a consecration on Mount Mahendraparvata 'in 802', a consecration that 'set the foundation of the Angkor period'; the Khmer Empire page: 'lasted from 802 to 1431 AD'. Cliopatria starts the state in 800; the page gives no month.

region.text: Land (Upper) Chenla, the northern lands

ledger.note: 803: the Chenla lands join Jayavarman II. he returned 'to his home in the former kingdom of Chenla' and defeated 'a series of competing kings' (undated); the page is silent on Land Chenla by name. The year is a bridge: Land Chenla's dossier is drawn through 802 and Cliopatria draws the union only from 806.

region.text: Water (Lower) Chenla, the southern lands to the Mekong delta

ledger.note: 803: Water Chenla joins. 'invaded and conquered the Water Chenla and beheaded Mahipativarman' (Java, before Jayavarman II was installed); he married the queen regnant of Sambhupura 'in order to unite Cambodia under one king' (undated). Water Chenla's own dossier ends c. 790; the page has him declaring war 'to expel the Javanese from Cambodia' in 'the later years (790-800)'. So 803 is a bridge. Reviewer se-01-c: counterpart changed from water-chenla, whose dossier ends c. 790 under Java with successor srivijaya; the Jayavarman II page: 'Jayavarman first remained subordinate to Java for some time and thereafter declared independence'.
c. 835: the court moves from Mahendraparvata to Hariharalaya near Roluos ('founded in the following years' after 802; infobox 'mid 9th century'). The year is a bridge between the two phrases.

region.text: the strip east of about 107 E that Cliopatria's Khmer shape of 806 shares with Champa's shape of 875

ledger.note: 875: the Khmer shape loses its eastern strip to Champa. The Khmer-Cham wars page treats Kauthara and Panduranga as Cham-held and is silent on 875; the year and the highlands-and-coast strip (about 45,800 km2 between 106.9 and 109 E) are Cliopatria's, where Champa grows from 77,900 to 130,300 km2 the same year.
889: the court settles at Yasodharapura (Angkor), founded under Yasovarman I, 'reigned 889-915'; infobox 'Yasodharapura (late 9th century-928)'.
928: Jayavarman IV moves the capital to Lingapura (Koh Ker), infobox 'Lingapura (928-944)'.
944: Rajendravarman II restores Yasodharapura as the capital, infobox 'Yasodharapura (944-1431)'.

region.text: Lavo, the Mon lands of the Menam valley (page: Rāmaññadesa)

ledger.note: 946: Angkor gained Rāmaññadesa 'in 946' (Sukhothai Kingdom page). Which land Rāmaññadesa means there is my reading (the Mon country of the Menam valley, here taken as Lavo); the Lavo dossier gives 946 as a vassalage date from its own page. Drawn as a tributary tint until Lavo is annexed in 1006. Reviewer se-01-c: the Lavo Kingdom page's infobox reads 'Angkor vassal: 946–1052' and the page says Lavo 'was then devastated by Angkor from the east in 946 and 1001'; source moved there, confidence 2.

region.text: Lavo

ledger.note: 1006: Lavo stops being a tributary and is governed from Angkor (annexation, next event).

region.text: Lavo, Lopburi and the Menam basin

ledger.note: 1006: Suryavarman I takes Lavo. 'Suryavarman expanded his territory to the west to Lopburi' and 'the Menam basin' (no year on the page); infobox reign 1006-1050 ('claimed the throne in 1010'; 'usurped King Udayadityavarman I ... in approximately 1002'). The year is the reign's start and the Lavo dossier's; Cliopatria draws the gain in 1028.

region.text: Lavo

ledger.note: 1052: Lavo returns to a ruler of its own. 'Suryavarman died in 1050' (page); the page is silent on 1052, which is the Lavo dossier's date (Haripunjaya's prince); Cliopatria's Khmer shape drops Lavo in 1056. Reviewer se-01-c: the Lavo Kingdom page's infobox dates it: 'Reclaimed by Suphannabhum/ Haripuñjaya: 1052' (and 'Angkor vassal: 946–1052'); source moved there, confidence 2.

region.text: Nghệ An, briefly seized in 1132

ledger.note: 1132: Khmer and Cham armies together 'briefly seized Nghệ An and raided Thanh Hoá's coast' against Đại Việt (Suryavarman II's second attempt after the 1128 rout at Nghệ An). Cliopatria's 'Ngô Dynasty' row stands for Đại Việt under the Lý.

region.text: Nghệ An and the frontier between Angkor and Đại Việt

ledger.note: 1136: a Vietnamese force of 30,000 under Đỗ Anh Vũ counterattacks into Khmer territory and retreats; the Cham make peace with Đại Việt and refuse to join Suryavarman's next attack, which fails. The page gives no treaty; no land changes hands.

region.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa' (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam)

ledger.note: 1145: Suryavarman II invades Champa, sacks Vijaya and deposes Jaya Indravarman III ('The Khmers held Vijaya until 1149', Khmer Empire page).

region.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa' (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam)

ledger.note: 1149: Jaya Harivarman I besieges Vijaya and defeats Prince Harideva at Mahisa; 'This ended Khmer occupation of northern Champa'.

region.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1177: a Cham fleet sails up the Mekong to the Tonlé Sap, sacks Yasodharapura and kills King Tribhuvanadityavarman; 'The Cham then occupied Cambodia for about four years'. Recorded by the owner, with the roles reversed; the month is not on this page.

region.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1181: Jayavarman VII wins a decisive naval battle and expels the Cham; he is crowned king the same year ('in 1181 was crowned king himself', Jayavarman VII page).

region.text: Lavo, Lopburi

ledger.note: 1181: Lavo comes under Angkor again. The page lists Lavo among the 23 towns where Jayavarman VII set up Buddha images ('Among them were Lavo (modern Lopburi)') and does not call it a conquest or a vassal; the Lavo dossier dates the governorship to 1181. The year is the coronation year, a bridge.

region.text: the Tak and upper Ping lands in the south of Haripunjaya's 1187 outline

ledger.note: 1188: the southern lands of Haripunjaya (Tak and the upper Ping) pass to Angkor in Cliopatria's shapes; the page is silent on any such conquest and the Haripunjaya dossier records the same event at conf 1. Placed in Jayavarman VII's reign (1181-1218).

region.text: the Mekong valley north to Vientiane, the Khorat plateau and the Kra Isthmus: the 1188 shape without the 1111 shape, Lavo and Haripunjaya

ledger.note: 1188: Jayavarman VII's empire reaches its widest extent short of Champa: he 'expanded Khmer control of the Mekong Valley northward to Vientiane' and 'southward down the Kra Isthmus'; infobox area 1,000,000 km2 for 1181-1218. The pages give no year for these steps; 1188 is Cliopatria's. The 830,253 km2 shape reaches 21.2 N, beyond Vientiane (18.0 N), which no opened page supports.

region.text: Vijaya, the Cham capital near Bình Định

ledger.note: 1190: Jayavarman VII's army under the Cham prince Vidyanandana 'defeated the Chams, occupied Vijaya, and captured Jaya Indravarman IV'; the Khmer Empire table dates the conquest 1190-1191.

region.text: Vijaya

ledger.note: 1191: a revolt at Vijaya drives out Suryajayavarman; Vidyanandana retakes it, kills the two Jaya Indravarmans and 'declared independence from the Khmer Empire'.

region.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa' (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam)

ledger.note: 1192: Jayavarman VII's invasions of Champa begin: 'repeated invasions' in 1192, 1195, 1198-1199 and 1201-1203. The page names Champa and Vijaya; the zone (northern Champa) is my reading.

region.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa' (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam)

ledger.note: 1203: after 22 years of war the Khmer 'conquered large parts of their territory' (Khmer Empire page); the Chams are defeated, Vidyanandana flees to Đại Việt and a puppet government is set up.

region.text: the whole of Champa, as Cliopatria's 1188 shape draws it

ledger.note: 1203: Champa becomes a Khmer province. 'Champa became a Khmer province ruled by a puppet government (Dhanapatigräma, then Angsaräja)' for 1203-1220. Cliopatria draws the shape from 1206 and the Champa dossier ends its drawing in 1202.

region.text: Lavo, Lopburi

ledger.note: 1218: Lavo leaves Angkor. 'Jayavarman died around 1218' and 'He was succeeded by Indravarman II, who died by 1243'; the pages opened say nothing about Lavo afterwards. The year is the Lavo dossier's ('Angkor 1181-1218; Phraek Si Racha 1218-1351'); Cliopatria keeps Lavo in the Khmer shape until 1240.

region.text: the whole of Champa, as Cliopatria's 1220 shape draws it

ledger.note: 1220: the Khmer withdraw from Champa. 'The Khmer voluntarily evacuated Champa'; Angsaräja takes power peacefully as Jaya Paramesvaravarman II (Khmer Empire page: 'withdrew from many provinces previously taken from the Chams' under pressure from Đại Việt and Champa).

region.text: the Sukhothai lands and the Chao Phraya valley west of the Khmer heartland

ledger.note: 1238: Sukhothai breaks away. 'Sukhothai is conventionally regarded as having emerged as an independent polity in 1238 CE': Bang Klang Hao (Si Inthrathit) took the city 'in 1238 with military help from his brother-in-law Pha Mueang'. The Khmer Empire page also puts a 'loss of western territories to Sukhothai' under Indravarman II (1219-1243), undated. The page contests the old 'liberation' story; the land is Cliopatria's Sukhothai shape (916 cells), my reading. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1241.

region.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1353: Angkor falls to Ayutthaya. 'Uthong besieged Angkor' in 1352; Angkor was captured 'the next year' and Siamese princes were installed as kings (the page's 1352-53; other sources give 1351). Recorded by the owner, with the roles reversed.

region.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1357: Suryavamsa Rajadhiraja retakes the throne and ends the Siamese rule at Angkor.

region.text: the northern Khmer lands (Isan north of the Mun and the Mekong valley), as Cliopatria draws their loss

ledger.note: 1363: the northern lands pass to Lan Xang in Cliopatria's shapes. The Khmer Empire page says Fa Ngum, exiled at Angkor, 'received a Khmer army to create a buffer state in Laos' and gives 'Lan Xang founded: 1353' on the infobox; it does not say the Khmer ceded land. Year and land are Cliopatria's (731 of the 733 cells lost lie in its Lan Xang shape).

region.text: the western strip of the Khmer realm that Cliopatria hands to Ayutthaya

ledger.note: 1375: a western strip passes to Ayutthaya in Cliopatria's shapes (212 of the 215 cells lost lie in its Ayutthaya shape of 1375). The page dates no cession in 1375; it dates sieges of Angkor in 1352-53 and 1393-94 and says Ayutthaya 'succeeded' Lavo, a 'former Khmer dependency', without a year.

region.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1393: Ramesuan of Ayutthaya besieges Angkor.

region.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1394: Angkor is captured by Ayutthaya; the page does not say how long the Siamese held it or on what terms.

region.text: the Khmer realm of 1431, which continues under Ponhea Yat at Phnom Penh (Chaktomuk)

ledger.note: 1431: Angkor falls and the Khmer Empire ends. 'Ponhea Yat abandoned Angkor as indefensible' and moved to the Phnom Penh area (the page adds that a line of kings may have stayed at Angkor); infobox 'Fall of Angkor: 1431', 'lasted from 802 to 1431 AD'. The Khmer state goes on at Phnom Penh as the separate dossier post-angkor-cambodia from 1432.

wars.name: Khmer-Cham war of c. 950
wars.outcome: Rajendravarman II's army pillaged the Po Nagar temple at Kauthara and took its golden Bhagavati statue, but the invasion ended in a 'bloody defeat'; Champa kept Kauthara. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Khmer Empire page gives 946 in its table and 950 in its text for the first war with Champa.

wars.name: Khmer-Cham war of 1074-1080
wars.outcome: A Khmer army attacked Vijaya and other northern Cham centres in 1080 and was driven out by Harivarman IV, whose raiders later reached Sambor and the Mekong. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Suryavarman II's wars against Đại Việt

zones.text: Nghệ An, invaded in 1128 and briefly seized in 1132

wars.outcome: A Khmer force of 20,000 was routed in Nghệ An in 1128; with Cham help the Khmer briefly took Nghệ An in 1132; a Vietnamese counterattack in 1136 and the Cham peace with Đại Việt ended the effort. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Cliopatria's 'Ngô Dynasty' row stands for Đại Việt under the Lý.

wars.name: Khmer invasion of Champa (Suryavarman II)

zones.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa' (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam)

wars.outcome: Suryavarman II sacked Vijaya in 1145 and the Khmer held northern Champa until Jaya Harivarman I retook Vijaya in 1149; he killed the pretender Vamsaraja at Mỹ Sơn in 1150.
wars.note: The Khmer-Cham wars page dates the Khmer defeats at Rajapura and Virapura to 1147-1148 with uncertain locations.

wars.name: Cham invasion of the Khmer Empire

zones.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

wars.outcome: A Cham land invasion in 1170 was inconclusive; in 1177 a Cham fleet sacked Yasodharapura and killed the king, and the Cham occupied Cambodia for about four years until Jayavarman VII's naval victory in 1181.

wars.name: Jayavarman VII's conquest of Champa

zones.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa' (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam)

wars.outcome: Vijaya was occupied in 1190-1191, then invaded in 1192, 1195, 1198-1199 and 1201-1203; Champa became a Khmer province under a puppet government in 1203 and the Khmer withdrew in 1220.
wars.note: A Khmer army with Burmese and Siamese mercenaries also fought the Đại Việt army in 1207 under Angsaräja (the page names no territorial result).

wars.name: Ayutthaya's sieges of Angkor (1352-1357)

zones.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

wars.outcome: Uthong besieged Angkor in 1352 and took it in 1353; Siamese princes ruled until Suryavamsa Rajadhiraja retook the throne in 1357.

wars.name: Ayutthaya's siege and capture of Angkor (1393-1394)

zones.text: Yasodharapura (Angkor) and the Tonlé Sap heartland

wars.outcome: Ramesuan besieged Angkor in 1393 and captured it in 1394; the page does not say how it was recovered.

wars.name: Siege of Angkor (1431)
wars.outcome: Ponhea Yat abandoned Angkor as indefensible and moved to the Phnom Penh area; the Khmer Empire ends and Post-Angkor Cambodia begins.
wars.note: The Post-Angkor period page calls it 'a Siamese intervention ... around the year 1431'.

certainty.note: Khmer frontiers were the reach of Angkor's governors and tributaries, not surveyed lines; the Cham coast, the Menam valley and the northern Mekong frontier are the softest. No treaty or survey on the pages opened fixes any line.

sources.title: Khmer Empire
sources.note: Identity, 802-1431, capitals, the 1,000,000 km2 area (1181-1218), the Cham and Siamese wars, Sukhothai, Lan Xang, the fall of Angkor in 1431.

sources.title: Khmer-Cham wars
sources.note: Every dated Cham war from c. 950 to 1220: the occupations of 1145-1149, 1177-1181 and 1190-1191, the conquest of 1203, the evacuation of 1220, the Đại Việt war of 1127-1136.

sources.title: Jayavarman II
sources.note: 802 consecration at Mahendraparvata; Water Chenla, Sambhupura, Hariharalaya; page silent on borders and on Land Chenla.

sources.title: Suryavarman I
sources.note: Reign 1006-1050; west to Lopburi and the Menam basin, no year; page silent on Champasak, Sukhothai and the extent at his death.

sources.title: Jayavarman VII
sources.note: 1181 coronation, death c. 1218, Vientiane, Kra Isthmus, Lavo among 23 towns; page silent on area and on the Champa years.

sources.title: Sukhothai Kingdom
sources.note: 1238 as the conventional independence of Sukhothai, the contested Khmer-liberation story, 946 Rāmaññadesa, Lavo and the Chao Phraya plain.

sources.title: Lavo Kingdom
sources.note: Added by the se-01-c reviewer: infobox 'Angkor vassal: 946–1052', the source of the 946 vassal_start.

notes:
Cliopatria row split. The 'Khmer Empire' row runs 800-1867 (28 shapes). This dossier takes 800-1431 (the Angkor empire, 15 Cliopatria shapes plus two new keyframes); the post-Angkor kingdom, 1432-1863, is the new dossier post-angkor-cambodia, which reviews the same row's later shapes (the 1375 shape is split between the two at 1431/1432).

Pages: nine opened for the whole row (Khmer Empire, Khmer-Cham wars, Jayavarman II, Suryavarman I, Jayavarman VII, Sukhothai Kingdom here; Post-Angkor period, Nam tien, French protectorate of Cambodia in the other dossier) = the page budget. Not opened: the Lavo, Haripunjaya, Ayutthaya, Lan Xang, Champa pages (other dossiers cite them). Every WebFetch was asked for the dated sentences; quotations in notes are the page's own words as returned.

What the pages did not settle (conf 1 events and 'page silent'): when the Chenla lands joined (803 is a bridge: Land Chenla's dossier is drawn through 802, Cliopatria joins them in 806); the 875 loss of the eastern strip to Champa (45,800 km2 of the 806 shape lies inside Champa's 875 shape); the 1006 and 1052 Lavo dates (the Suryavarman I page gives no year for the westward expansion; the Lavo dossier's dates are used so the gain and loss pair up); the 1188 step (the Haripunjaya lands and the stateless uplands) and the 1188 northern edge (21.2 N, beyond Vientiane at 18.0 N, unsupported); the 1363 loss to Lan Xang (the page says a Khmer army helped found it) and the 1375 loss to Ayutthaya (the page dates no cession).

Corrections made to Cliopatria's shapes: start 802 instead of 800 with the core only for 802; the Chenla union from 803; Lavo inside the Khmer shape 1006-1051 and 1181-1217 instead of 1028-1055 and 1188-1240 (to match the Lavo dossier); Champa inside 1203-1219 instead of 1206-1219; Sukhothai lost from 1238 instead of 1241. Infobox area check: 1,000,000 km2 for 1181-1218 against 830,253 (1188) and 953,197 (1206): ratios 0.83 and 0.95.

Left out on purpose: Sulaiman's 851 story that the Khmer 'became a vassal of the Sailendra dynasty' (the page calls it legend); the 916 report of a Javanese king executing the Khmer king; tribute to the Mongols from 1285 and the 'devastated' country in August 1296 after a recent war with the Siamese (Zhou Daguan; no date or land); Chinese sources adding Pegu to the empire in 1195 (the land is inside Pagan's Cliopatria shape and no other page confirms it; not drawn); the Khmer conquest claims of the Siamese chronicles for the Menam valley are Pagan-side claims. The 946 'vassal' of Lavo rests on the Sukhothai page's 'Angkor gained Rāmaññadesa in 946', a Mon-country reading, conf 1. Rulers are omitted: the pages opened give reign dates that disagree (Jayavarman II 802-850 or 802-835; Jayavarman VII ends 1218 or 1219).

Needs from others: ayutthaya-kingdom and lan-xang should carry the matching gain events (1375, 1363) and the occupation of Angkor 1353-1357 / 1393-1394; sukhothai-kingdom the 1238 gain; champa the 875 gain (its dossier has 757); lavo-kingdom already has 1006, 1052, 1181, 1218; haripunjaya the 1188 loss. Counterparts without a dossier: none in this file except 'nobody' for the 1188 uplands.

Gazetteer names used: 'Angkor (region)', Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quàng Nam, Nghệ An, Vijaya. No unknown names.
